thread:
anya: quick heads-up — onboarding norse-2.1 (mistral-derivative) shows periodic hallucination artifacts in long-context QA runs, repeating every ~512 tokens
samir: ugh. artifact period == typical rotary wrap for our config? seen logs?
anya: pasting small decode sample:
```
Q: When did X happen?
A: It happened in 19XX...
... repeats similar phrase at tokens 512, 1024
```

olga: could be tokenizer id mapping mismatch vs llama-format checkpoint. last time we saw wrap-like artifacts it was a tokenid offset + rope misalignment.
anya: that was my suspicion. On export from HF -> our binary we ran `tokenizer.save_pretrained()` then a tiny converter. I noticed converter uses `int.from_bytes(..., 'little')` but HF indices assumed big-endian. didn’t think much of it.
samir: oh nice catch. so some token ids might be byte-swapped during serialization? that would reorder vocab indices but keep merge-pairs identical -> aliasing.
kim: if token ids shift, rotary phase which multiplies by token_pos will be applied to the wrong embeddings headwise. leads to consistent periodic phase errors. matches the 512 periodicity.
olga: repro plan: 1) run tokenizer roundtrip id check: compare hf_ids vs converter_ids for first 100k tokens. 2) run a tiny forward-only model with both tokenmaps and diff logits and kv cache.
anya: ran step 1 quickly: ~0.3% tokens had id xor 0x01000000 pattern (byte-swapped). attached snippet:
```
# sample rows (index, hf_id, conv_id)
0, 743, 743
1, 1024, 16777216
2, 1025, 1025
...2, 65536 -> 1 (byte reorder)
```

ci-bot: ci/presubmit tokenmap-check failing on norse-2.1-converter (test: token_endian_consistency). See logs: https://ci.redwood/norse/1234
samir: thanks. that pattern explains aliasing + rope head offsets. short-term patch: change converter to use big-endian int decoding and re-run quant. Also add a unit test that asserts id roundtrip for top-200k tokens.
kim: longer term we should make tokenizer format explicit (endianness field) and version-check during model bring-up to avoid silent passes. Also consider adding a stage to our onboarding: tokenmap-consistency + rope-phase-sanity test (run 2-3 synthetic prompts and check for repeating periodic artifacts).
anya: I’ll send a PR for the converter and add the test to presubmit. tagging @samir for kv-cache diff harness — can you run the two-maps logits diff after I push?
samir: will do. if it still reproduces after fix we’ll dig into headwise rotary scaling differences (Gemma->Qwen parity). but this looks like byte-order bug.
olga: documenting: root cause hypothesis = tokenizer export used system-native endianness when writing int32 ids -> ended up inconsistent across OSes/py versions.
anya: action items: PR converter + unit test (anya), run presubmit + kv-cache logits-diff (samir), add tokenizer-endianness metadata to onboarding checklist (olga/kim). thanks everyone :thumbsup:
